problem:
Calculate the Cartesian equation of the circle

$$
x=7\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=7\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi .
$$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14011969/assets/20c1f81e9737856b7cf1fbf031fd42988a37eb418303114d95f6521c0401fa61.png)

Consider the circle of radius $2$ centered at $(4,-3)$, as shown above. Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$  traverse the circle once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(6,-3)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a circle of radius $r$ centered at the point $(a,b)$ are

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +a,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +b,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the circle is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(r+a,b).$

In our case, we have a circle of radius $2$ centered at the point $(4,-3).$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the circle are

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
